name: Amba
role: Princess of Kashi in the Mahabharata
summary: Amba is the eldest princess of Kashi in the Mahabharata. After her svayamvara is disrupted by Bhishma, she vows to see him fall and is said to be reborn as Shikhandi.
about: In the Mahabharata, Amba is the eldest of three princesses of Kashi, with sisters Ambika and Ambalika. At their svayamvara, Bhishma takes the three sisters for his half-brother Vichitravirya. Amba says she had chosen King Salva, but Salva turns her away. Bhishma cannot marry her because of his vow. Amba seeks the help of Parashurama, whose duel with Bhishma ends in a draw, and she then does hard penance. The epic says Shiva grants her a boon to be reborn as the one who will bring about Bhishma's end. In the tellings, she is reborn as Shikhandi, a child of King Drupada, who fights at Kurukshetra. Versions differ in some details, such as the lotus garland from Kartikeya.
kidSummary: Amba was a princess of Kashi in the Mahabharata. Her wedding plans were interrupted, and she felt very hurt. She prayed with great determination, and the story says she was reborn as Shikhandi to keep her vow. Her tale is about strong feelings and fairness.

story.title: Three princesses
story.text: The king of Kashi holds a svayamvara for his three daughters. Amba hopes to choose King Salva, whom she loves.

story.title: Bhishma arrives
story.text: Bhishma takes the three sisters to Hastinapura for his half-brother. When Amba explains her wish, he lets her go to Salva.

story.title: A closed door
story.text: Salva turns her away, saying that Bhishma won her. Bhishma also cannot marry her because of his vow. Amba is left without a home.

story.title: Seeking help
story.text: Amba asks Parashurama, Bhishma's teacher, for help. The duel lasts 23 days and ends in a draw on the twenty-fourth. Amba does long penance.

story.title: A new birth
story.text: In the story, Shiva promises her a rebirth. She is born as Shikhandi, and at Kurukshetra Bhishma lowers his weapons when he sees Shikhandi.

teaches: Perseverance in the face of hardship
Understanding how decisions affect other people

facts.text: In the Udyoga Parva account, Bhishma and Parashurama fought for 23 days with no winner. On the 24th, as Bhishma reached for a deadly weapon, Narada and the gods asked Parashurama to stop, and the duel was declared a draw.

Amba stood still for six months in the Yamuna valley, living on air alone. Later she balanced on tiptoe, eating a single fallen leaf. After twelve years, her penance was said to scorch the heavens and the earth.

In the Udyoga Parva, Ganga cursed Amba to become a crooked river, dry for eight months and flowing only in the rains. Half of Amba became the river in Vatsa, while the other half stayed human because of her ascetic merit.
In one version of the story, the god Kartikeya gave Amba a garland of ever-fresh blue lotuses that would help whoever wore it defeat Bhishma.

In the Udyoga Parva, a yaksha named Sthunakarna briefly exchanged sexes with Shikhandi when her marriage led to a conflict with another kingdom. Kubera later cursed him to stay in the changed form until Shikhandi's death.
Before collapsing, Bhishma cried out that it was Arjuna's arrows that had killed him, not Shikhandi's. He then lay on a bed of arrows, which in the tellings fulfils Amba's vow.
Amba thought over who was to blame for her plight: Bhishma who abducted her, Salva who rejected her, her father who arranged the svayamvara, and even herself for not escaping the chariot.
Amba's story is the Ambopakhyana in the Udyoga Parva, and Bhishma himself tells it to Duryodhana to explain why he will not kill Shikhandi.
Amba is an everyday Sanskrit word for 'mother', and in Vedic usage it is linked to the mother of the Vedas.
Amba also appears in Javanese wayang, the shadow-puppet theatre, where a puppet of her is shown on her Wikipedia page.
At the svayamvara Salva challenged Bhishma to a duel. Bhishma beat him and wounded him but spared his life, then drove off the other kings who chased his chariot.
In another version, Bhishma asked Vichitravirya to marry Amba, but he refused because she loved someone else. She was now turned away by three bachelors.
Amba begged many kings to defeat Bhishma for her, but all declined because they knew how strong he was.
In the retelling on Amba's page, Shiva promised the childless Drupada a child who would be born a girl and later become a boy, which is how her rebirth as Shikhandi is explained.
Shikhandi was raised as a boy and married the daughter of King Hiranyavarna of Dasharna. When the secret came out, he declared war on Panchala.
On the Kurukshetra field, the Pandavas set Shikhandi before Bhishma because, as Amba, she had won a promise that he would lay down his weapons on seeing her.
The Amba article says Shikhandi's arrows did not wound Bhishma, who himself wished to die, so he fell only after Arjuna's arrows struck.
Bhishma stayed on his bed of arrows for 51 days, teaching the Pandavas. He taught the Vishnu Sahasranama before dying on the day of Uttarayana, the winter solstice.
In the garland version, Amba hung the lotus garland on a pillar outside Drupada's palace, and the text says no one dared to touch it.
Shikhandi was killed on the last night of the war in a sword fight with Ashvatthama, when Ashvatthama, Kripa and Kritavarma raided the Pandava camp.

quiz.q: Who did Amba hope to marry?
quiz.why: Amba loved King Salva and planned to choose him.

quiz.q: For how many days did Bhishma and Parashurama fight with no winner?
quiz.why: They fought for 23 days with no winner, and on the 24th day the duel was declared a draw.

quiz.q: Who is Amba reborn as in the Mahabharata?
quiz.why: Amba is said to be reborn as Shikhandi.

quiz.q: Which god granted Amba a boon in the epic?
quiz.why: Shiva gave her the boon of rebirth.

quiz.q: What does the word Amba mean?
quiz.why: Amba is an old word for mother.
